key_insight: A biologically informed dual-branch transformer separates a cell's baseline state from drug-induced regulatory shifts, enabling accurate prediction of transcriptional responses across nonlinear dose–time trajectories and unseen cellular contexts.
problem_solved: Predicting how cells' gene expression changes after drug perturbations across varying doses, times and cell types while disentangling intrinsic cell state from treatment effects to improve generalization and interpretability.
method: Dual-branch transformer: one branch encodes baseline cell/state features, the other encodes drug-induced perturbation signals; outputs are combined to predict post-treatment transcriptional profiles.
Explicit dose and time embeddings plus attention mechanisms capture nonlinear dose–time dynamics and interactions with regulatory programs.
Biologically informed training objectives and latent disentanglement encourage separation of intrinsic cell state vs. treatment effect, improving transfer to unseen cell contexts.
impact: Provides a generalizable, interpretable modeling paradigm for perturbation prediction useful in drug discovery, perturbation screening and transfer learning; demonstrates how architectural inductive biases (biological priors + transformers) improve real-world generalization.
visual_elements: Schematic of the dual-branch transformer showing separate baseline and perturbation branches, fusion layer, and predicted gene expression output
Dose–time response plots illustrating nonlinear trajectories and model fit vs. ground truth
Latent-space visualization (e.g., UMAP) separating baseline cell-state embeddings from drug-shift embeddings to show disentanglement
Heatmap comparison of observed vs. predicted gene expression across conditions (including unseen cell types)
paper_title: Modelling drug-induced cellular perturbation responses with a biologically informed dual-branch transformer
paper_authors: Yue Guo, Hao Zhang, Haitao Hu, Jialu Wu, Ji Cao
